Telescope 4.0 is the biggest update since 3.0. The desktop app is a lot lighter while streaming and got a new look with a proper Settings window. Auto framing and background blur arrive as optional plugins and streaming is much smoother when the Wi-Fi isn't great. There's nothing to do before upgrading and your pairings and settings carry over.

## New

**Lighter on your computer.** The desktop app uses up to 50% less CPU while streaming and on Linux up to 75% less RAM. Memory used to keep creeping up during long sessions and now it stays about where it started.

**A new look.** This refines the look 3.0 brought in, card by card. The goal was a window that's easier to use and quicker to scan, and one you can use entirely from the keyboard, which makes Telescope a lot more accessible too. Checkboxes became switches, resolution and frame rate are tiles and every card has its own colour (**Monochrome** under **Card colours** in General puts them all back in purple). Tab goes through everything in reading order, focus rings show up when you're using the keyboard and every control has a name for screen readers.

**One Settings window.** The settings button in the top right opens a single window with tabs instead of a menu full of pop-ups, and what used to be in Advanced is spread over those tabs now. Every tab uses the same one row per setting layout with shorter tooltips. The search box finds a setting by its name or by what it does, even with a typo in it.

**Folding cards.** Click a card's title to fold it down to its header, or a section title like **Focus** to fold just that part. It works from the keyboard too and what you fold stays folded after a restart.

**Auto framing and Background.** Auto framing moves the zoom and pan to follow you, widens when you hold a hand out to show something and zooms back out when nobody's there. While it's moving the picture the phone waits until it settles before switching lenses. Background blurs what's behind you or swaps it for a picture. They're the first plugins that stay off until you switch them on under **Optional** in Settings → Plugins, which downloads the vision models they need (about 47 MB on Linux and 28 MB on Windows).

**A better Browser camera.** It now uses the device's own video hardware where the browser offers it, which is easier on the battery and gives a smoother, more reliable picture. It also starts streaming almost right after the page connects. Its card shows what the browser is really sending, and the page got a Light button that turns on the flash (or a white screen for the front camera).

**UDP on Wi-Fi (experimental).** A switch in the Connection card sends Light over UDP. On busy Wi-Fi a lost packet then only means resending that one piece instead of holding up the whole stream. If nothing gets through (usually a firewall) it goes back to TCP. It doesn't work with Dynamic or Heavy yet. My own Wi-Fi is too quiet to show a difference so I'd love to hear how it does on a crowded one.

**Hardware acceleration.** A switch in Settings → Video decodes Light on the graphics card, mostly worth it at 4K or on a laptop. AMD and Intel cards on Linux need VA-API and **Set up VA-API…** next to the switch gets it for you. I couldn't try it on Windows with a real graphics card so please report it if it doesn't work there.

**Auto level** in the Microphone card evens out quiet and loud speech without turning up the room noise in the pauses.

## Smoother streaming

- No more mic clicks when the phone's clock and the computer's drift apart, and less mic delay overall.
- Plugging in the cable mid-stream moves to USB without a gap.
- The phone uses H.264's High profile when it can, which looks a bit sharper at the same bitrate.
- Where the phone's encoder can do it the picture gets refreshed bit by bit instead of in one big burst every second, which is easier on busy Wi-Fi.
- Dynamic handles really slow links better and changes the frame rate without restarting the camera.
- A phone that gets too hot lowers its frame rate instead of heating up until the alert stops the stream.
- The phone keeps its screen and Wi-Fi awake while Telescope is open to avoid lag spikes (the power button still turns the screen off).
- Streams start a little sooner and recover about a second faster after a Wi-Fi drop.
- **Can't keep up** says when a weak signal or 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi is the reason, and it no longer shows up when the Wi-Fi drops out completely.

## Fixed

- The phone mic stayed quiet after Android's audio system restarted.
- The phone app sometimes couldn't be found after it was reopened quickly.
- Stopping on the phone and leaving the app right away showed up on the desktop as a dropped stream.
- Saved keyboard shortcuts and arrow key panning didn't work, and the shortcuts plugin could crash.
- Overwriting a preset lost the settings of plugins that were switched off.
- Some windows opened behind the main window.

## For plugin makers

- Plugins put their settings in the Settings window with `create_settings_sections()`. The old `create_menu_actions()` still works (its entries show up under the plugin's name in General) but it's deprecated.

Keep the phone app and the desktop on the same version since most of this needs both. Found something broken? Open an issue and paste your **Copy diagnostics** report into it.
